solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A black horse, caught entering a monk's office

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: one piece going into another, so the letter for caught is placed within the horse

parts.note: a bay is a reddish-brown horse
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A dark horse is caught wandering into a monastery official's room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' puts C inside BAY to give BACY, after A and B.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbacy is the post or jurisdiction of an abbot, the monk who heads an abbey.

clue.text: Cautionary signal recognised at first by doctor in A&E

indicators.note: the doctor is placed within the letters of the department

parts.note: the letters A and E, as in the hospital's Accident and Emergency department
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word recognised is wanted

explanation.surface: A warning sign is spotted early by a doctor working in the emergency department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts MB between A and E to give AMBE, then 'at first' adds R from 'recognised'. A&E is the British hospital casualty department.
explanation.definitionFit: On traffic lights the yellow-orange light warns drivers to stop, so it is a cautionary signal.

clue.text: Horse trials venue using inferior porcelain?

parts.note: something bad is of poor or inferior quality
Minton is a famous English pottery and porcelain maker

explanation.surface: A horse event held at a place that serves on cheap china.
explanation.walkthrough: Badminton, a Gloucestershire estate, hosts a famous British three-day equestrian event; Minton is an English china brand.
explanation.definitionFit: The Badminton Horse Trials are held each spring on the Duke of Beaufort's estate in England.

clue.text: Youngster consuming hot fish

indicators.note: eating up another piece, so the letter for hot goes inside the youngster

parts.note: a cub is a young animal, or a junior scout
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A child eats a spicy fish dish.
explanation.definitionFit: The chub is a freshwater fish of the carp family, popular with anglers.

clue.text: Pampered head of science group in school

indicators.note: these pieces go within the school

parts.note: a coed is a coeducational school, for boys and girls together

indicators.note: only the leading letter of science is wanted

parts.note: a set is a group of things or people

explanation.surface: A spoilt leader of a science class at a mixed school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of' gives S, which with SET goes 'in' COED.
explanation.definitionFit: To cosset is to spoil or indulge someone, so the past participle means spoilt or indulged.

clue.text: Leaving tip, avoiding busy periods

parts.note: to be off is to be leaving or departing
a peak is the tip or top of something

explanation.surface: Going without leaving a gratuity, to dodge the rush hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-peak travel or electricity is used outside the times of greatest demand, when it is quieter and cheaper.

clue.text: She marks Old English exercises? Cobblers!

indicators.note: letters that are exercised are worked over and moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A teacher grades Anglo-Saxon homework and finds it rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cobblers!' looks like British slang for nonsense, the teacher's verdict, but it is the definition in its literal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobblers are people who make and mend footwear, the same trade under another name.

clue.text: Little can keep yours truly subdued

indicators.note: to hold or keep within, so the speaker's pronoun goes inside the small amount

parts.note: a tad is a little bit
yours truly is a jokey way of saying me

explanation.surface: A small tin may keep a letter-writer quietened.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tamed has been brought under control, broken in or subdued.

clue.text: Manure a Welshman collected — wearing these?

definitions.text: Manure a Welshman collected — wearing these?

parts.note: dung is animal manure
Rees is a common Welsh surname, standing for a Welshman

explanation.surface: A Welsh farmer gathers muck, and the question is what he wore to do it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the scene and also builds the word: the farmhand gathering muck would wear the work overalls.
explanation.definitionFit: Dungarees are hard-wearing bib overalls, the natural clothing for a farmhand shovelling muck.

clue.text: Trendy pad son leaves for introduction of Oxford blue

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy

indicators.note: the son departs, so his letter is dropped from the lodgings

parts.note: digs and pad are both slang for lodgings

indicators.note: only the opening letter of Oxford is used

explanation.surface: A fashionable flat where a student son moves out in favour of an Oxford Blue sportsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford blue' reads as one phrase, a shade or a sporting honour, but Oxford only gives O and blue is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is a deep violet-blue colour, from the dye of that name.

clue.text: Arab nomad's base in Paris or Indiana

parts.note: a bed is a base or foundation, as in a river bed
ou is the French word for or
IN is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Indiana

explanation.surface: Asks where a desert wanderer is based, France or the American Midwest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bedouin are desert-dwelling Arab peoples who traditionally live as wandering herders.

clue.text: US investigator with mobile for underground worker

indicators.note: something mobile moves about, so these letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: a G-man is an FBI agent, short for government man

explanation.surface: An American agent carrying a phone stands in for a miner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobile' looks like a phone in the agent's hand but is the anagram signal on 'for'. The definition is loose: this diver works under water rather than underground.
explanation.definitionFit: A frogman is a diver in a wetsuit who works beneath the surface, here stretched to underground work.

clue.text: Good to abandon one form of control for another

indicators.note: the good letter leaves, so it is taken out of the word for rule

parts.note: a reign is rule by a monarch, a form of control

explanation.surface: A general remark on swapping one way of governing for a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' is the definition, meaning another form of control, carried over from the phrase before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rein is a strap used to steer a horse, a different means of keeping something in check.

clue.text: Aimed, perhaps, to present integrated methods of communication?

parts.note: the word aimed is one example of the letters of media in a jumbled order, so mixing media can give it

explanation.surface: Asks whether a targeted campaign uses several combined forms of communication.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer read as wordplay, MEDIA anagrammed, yields 'Aimed'; 'perhaps' marks it as just one possible result.
explanation.definitionFit: Mixed media is the use of several means of expression together, such as sound, text and image.

clue.text: Prepare calmly but with sadness

parts.note: to plan is to prepare in advance
gently means softly or calmly

explanation.surface: Getting ready serenely, but with a sorrowful heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Plangent describes a loud mournful sound, so the adverb means in a sorrowful, plaintive way.

clue.text: Bits of iron, mark, and other things with gold inside.

indicators.note: these pieces sit within the letters for mark

parts.note: MK is an abbreviation of mark, as in the old German currency
et al is short for the Latin et alia, and others
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A list of scrap: iron pieces, a mark, assorted items, some gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' sends the three middle pieces between the two letters for mark; 'with' is not a link here but stands for its own abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Metalwork means objects made of metal, so wrought pieces of iron are an example.

clue.text: Explosive device in writing about sick man keeping minutes

indicators.note: the manuscript letters go round the word for sick

parts.note: MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing
ill means sick

indicators.note: the man holds the letter for minutes within him

parts.note: Bob is a man's name

explanation.surface: A bomb hidden in a letter about an invalid, timed in minutes.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mills bomb was the British hand grenade of both World Wars.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mills bomb is a hand grenade, named after its designer William Mills.

clue.text: Draw along vessel, king having advantage

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
an edge is a slight advantage over a rival

explanation.surface: A monarch with the upper hand hauls a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To kedge is to move a ship by hauling on a small anchor dropped ahead of it.

clue.text: Orgiastic incident initiated in council upset Scotsman

indicators.note: the letter goes within the turned-round council
in a down clue, upset turns the word over, so council is read bottom to top

parts.note: a synod is a church council

indicators.note: only the first letter of incident is used

parts.note: Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A wild episode began at a meeting that rattled a Scot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the council upside down, as a down clue allows, and 'in' places the opening letter of 'incident' within it, before the Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: Dionysian, after Dionysus the Greek god of wine, describes wild, frenzied revelry.

clue.text: Revolutionary leader initially followed by figure from east

indicators.note: only the opening letter of leader is wanted
in an across clue, reading from the east means right to left

parts.note: nine is a figure, a number

explanation.surface: A rebel chief whose rise began with a follower from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from east' reads NINE backwards as ENIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenin led the Russian Bolshevik revolution of 1917, the archetypal revolutionary.

clue.text: Unresponsive, not very overbearing

indicators.note: the very letter is absent, so it comes out

parts.note: someone impervious is unmoved by or unresponsive to things

explanation.surface: A cold, aloof person who is not quite domineering.
explanation.definitionFit: An imperious person is arrogant and domineering, expecting to be obeyed.

clue.text: Supporting old president, prohibit a craft from the Far East

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting pieces sit underneath, so they come after the president

parts.note: Ike was the nickname of US President Dwight Eisenhower
to ban is to prohibit

explanation.surface: Backing a former leader, someone bans an Oriental art.
explanation.definitionFit: Ikebana is the Japanese art of flower arranging, a traditional craft of Japan.

clue.text: Woman originally producing house keys

indicators.note: only the first letter of producing is used

parts.note: E, B and E are musical keys

explanation.surface: A woman who first made spare house keys.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoebe is a woman's given name, also borne by a Titaness of Greek myth.

clue.text: With restricted credit, encase musical instrument

parts.note: a credit squeeze is a time when lending is restricted
to box is to put into a case or box

explanation.surface: Money is tight, so a musician packs the instrument away.
explanation.definitionFit: Squeezebox is the informal name for a concertina or accordion, played by squeezing the bellows.

clue.text: Typical American university man

parts.note: US stands for United States, so American
Al is a man's name

explanation.surface: A stereotypical American college fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Usual means normal or customary, the ordinary thing to expect.

clue.text: Reportedly not her expression of praise!

indicators.note: the word is heard spoken rather than seen written

parts.note: not her but the male pronoun, him

explanation.surface: A joking protest that a compliment went to him instead of her.
explanation.definitionFit: A song of praise to God is sung in church, a religious expression of worship.

clue.text: From Perelman, a humorous book?

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Suggests a comic book by the American humorist S. J. Perelman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' picks the letters out of 'Perelman, a humorous'; the question mark warns that the book is not comic but biblical.
explanation.definitionFit: Nahum is a short prophetic book of the Old Testament, among the Minor Prophets.

clue.text: Musical canon's duty list

definitions.meaning: a round, a piece in which voices enter in turn with the same tune, as in the old English song Sumer is icumen in
a schedule saying who works when

explanation.surface: A round of song turns out to be the work schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: Rota is an old name for a round sung in canon, and the everyday British word for a duty roster.

clue.text: Work unit moving a prickly plant

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work

indicators.note: letters that are moving shift around into a new order

explanation.surface: A work team carries a cactus about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges UNIT and A into UNTIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Opuntia is the prickly pear, a genus of cacti with spiny flat pads.

clue.text: Academic circle sure to be taken in by mistake

indicators.note: the circle and sure letters are absorbed within the slang for mistake

parts.note: bish is British slang for a mistake or blunder
O is a circle by its shape
OK means sure, as in agreement

explanation.surface: A scholar's ring, certain to be fooled by an error.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bookish is studious and fond of reading, much like an academic type.

clue.text: Pot youth leader is able to put beside cape

parts.note: a bill is a narrow headland or cape, as in Portland Bill on the Dorset coast

indicators.note: the first letter of youth leads the word

parts.note: can means is able to

explanation.surface: A youth group leader manages to set a pot down next to a cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cape' looks like a cloak but is the headland, as in Portland Bill on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A billycan is a metal cooking pot with a lid and handle, used over a campfire.

clue.text: Bottle Geordie's mother shows, catching large antelope

indicators.note: the mother holds the antelope inside her

parts.note: mam is the north-east English word for mum; a Geordie is someone from Newcastle
the gnu, or wildebeest, is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: A Tyneside mum displays a bottle while catching a wildebeest.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnum is a large wine bottle holding twice the standard amount, one and a half litres.
